data.narrative:
Cartesia is a Series B-stage AI & Software company that has raised $186M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public reference point (Palantir), with stage-adjacent comparables including Figure AI ($39.0B, Series C), Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A), Skild AI ($14.0B, Series C), Crusoe Energy ($10.0B, Series C), and Together AI ($8.3B, Series A).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $186M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $353M. Peer-median analysis across the 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $10.0B, with observed range spanning $3.2B to $39.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects the heterogeneity in AI company valuations at overlapping stages.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $300M (low) to $11.5B (high), with a median of $5.2B. The significant spread between stage-progression and peer-median methodologies reflects uncertainty around the appropriate valuation multiple for frontier-stage AI companies and the degree to which Cartesia's positioning maps to the observed peer set. Resolution of this range depends on clarity regarding revenue traction, model differentiation, and near-term commercial deployment relative to the comparable set.
